issues.description: Method Farm.addAnimal: the UML in problem_statement.md declares addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean (problem_statement.md line 18), but the reference implementation defines public void addAnimal(Animal animal) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 23). The task text (problem_statement.md line 109) describes addAnimal(Animal a) adds an animal to the list without specifying a return type, and the template file contains a TODO instead of a concrete signature (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 4). This inconsistency between the UML and the code/template can confuse students about whether to implement addAnimal to return a boolean (e.g., the result of animals.add(a)) or to make it void.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the UML (problem_statement.md) to declare addAnimal(Animal a): void and ensure the problem text and template reflect a void method; or (B) Change the template and solution to implement a boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) that returns animals.add(animal) (e.g., public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) { return animals.add(animal); }) and update the UML and task text to specify the boolean return. Also update the template to include the chosen method signature so students implement the expected return type and adjust any tests/documentation accordingly.
